title: Liberties
intro: Black and White take turns placing stones on the crossings of the lines. Stones stay where they are placed.
An empty crossing directly beside a stone is a liberty. Let's look at some on the board.

steps.instruction: Place a black stone on any empty crossing. The rings show its liberties.
steps.explanation: Liberties touch a stone above, below, left or right. Diagonal crossings do not count.

steps.instruction: Place a stone in a corner. Look at the rings beside it.
steps.hint: Any of the four corners of the board.
steps.explanation: An isolated corner stone has two liberties. An edge stone has three; a stone in the open has four.

steps.instruction: Join the two black stones by placing a stone directly below them.
steps.hint: Directly under the lowest black stone.
steps.explanation: Touching stones of the same colour form one group. The whole group shares its liberties.

outro: Next, try capturing a group by filling its last liberty.
